title: An exceptional component has an exceptional component in each nonempty specialized closure fibre
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth $X_\eta$ and etale $D_\eta$. Assume that $X$ is normal: every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ be a semistable $\eta$-modification. Let $s\in T$, let $C\subseteq Y_s$ be an irreducible component with generic point $z$, and let $W=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq Y$ with the reduced induced closed-subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Assume that $f_Y(C)$ is a point and that $C_{\overline{\kappa(s)}}\simeq\mathbf P^1_{\overline{\kappa(s)}}$ and meets the marking and singular locus of the geometric fibre in at most two points. For every specialization $t$ of $s$ for which $W_t$ is nonempty, there exists an irreducible component $C_t$ of $Y_t$ contained in $W_t$ such that $f_Y(C_t)$ is a point, $C_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\overline{\kappa(t)}\simeq\mathbf P^1_{\overline{\kappa(t)}}$, and this geometric component meets the marking and singular locus of the geometric fibre in at most two points. Specialization means membership in the closure of the singleton. Components have their reduced induced structures. This is a statement about a prescribed nonempty fibre of the closure of one component; it does not require its image point to be closed in $X$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Temkin, Lemma 4.4.4 proof AFTER the explicit replacement of the target by its normalization, printed pp. 31--32, referring to the normal-target compactification and genus argument of Lemma 4.4.2.
